must_fix.issue: A question held on a tail call never gets a Return if the remote releases our promise export while the named call is parked on it. Commit 908314b marks a `yourself` call when it arrives, so the redirect that names a parked call is now held. But when the remote's Release takes the promise export's refcount to 0, `destroyExportEntry` frees the parked calls and sends no Return. The parked call is never answered and its Finish never comes: rpc.capnp:489-492 and the C++ reference send Finish(Y) only after our Finish(X). So the held question X waits until a cancel, a deadline or disconnect. The `yourself` mark and the `active_inbound_questions` entry also leak. On main, X got the bare `takeFromOtherQuestion` at once: a Peer `unwrap()` error, or the native 'unsupported Return variant' EXCEPTION. The dropped call with no Return is pre-existing. The hang is new.

Silent drop: src/rpc/peer/peer_cap_lifecycle.zig:259-264 (destroyExportEntry calls deinit_pending_call with no Return; reached from releaseExport, releasePromiseHeldExport, releaseAnswerHeldExport and releaseHandoffHeldExport). Claims this breaks: docs/native-abi.md:42 ('Every question ends with exactly one RETURN effect'), docs/native-abi.md:79-88, CHANGELOG.md:107-111.
must_fix.why: The tail caller's question hangs with no RETURN, which breaks the one-Return-per-question rule. It is reachable from C++. A tail call to a cap the host passed as a promise export (capnp_promise_export) parks on our side. The C++ ImportClient is then dropped, as callNoIntercept does with releaseParams, or when the handler's temporary cap dies. C++ then sends Release. C++ itself keeps in-flight calls running after a Release: rpc.c++:4250 releaseExport only drops the export table's own reference.

must_fix.suggested_fix: Give every parked call a Return when its promise export is destroyed. For example, fail each call with sendReturnException(question_id, "promise export released") instead of only freeing it. A `yourself` call then goes through completeSelfLoopbackException: the held question gets the exception and the remote gets resultsSentElsewhere. Another option is to pin the promise export while calls are parked on it. At a minimum, when a parked `yourself` call is dropped, remove its mark and settle any hold on its id. Commit both probes as tests and check that they fail without the fix.

must_fix.issue: A tail call that names a call pipelined on a tail-called answer never ends. The C++ reference turns every call it forwards back over the same connection into a tail call: RpcClient::callNoIntercept calls directTailCall. That includes a call our app pipelined on a question X that C++ answered by tail-calling us (Y). C++ sends it to Y's PipelineClient as Call(W, sendResultsTo = yourself, target = promisedAnswer(Y)) plus Return(W0, takeFromOtherQuestion = W). planPromisedTarget queues every call whose answer is not in resolved_answers. A `yourself` answer is never recorded there, and completeSelfLoopbackReturn never drains pending_promises[Y]. So W is queued forever with no Return. Since 908314b, W is marked at arrival, so W0's redirect is held forever. This happens in both orders: Y answered before W arrives (a DIRECT handler) or after (a native host). On main, W0 got the bare tag at once. W stuck in the queue is pre-existing. W0 hanging is new.

C++: vendor/ext/capnproto/c++/src/capnp/rpc.c++:1126-1137 and 3373-3400. Claim this breaks: docs/native-abi.md:42.
must_fix.why: The pipelined question gets no RETURN at all. That breaks one Return per question, and it hangs the host's pipelined call. Promise pipelining through a reflected tail call is ordinary use. C++ supports it on purpose: 'the tail results could have caps, so we must continue to honor pipeline calls (and just bounce them back)'. Before, the host got an error at once.

must_fix.suggested_fix: When a `yourself` call is answered (completeSelfLoopbackReturn, either branch), fail the calls queued on it with failQueuedPromisedCalls(answer_id, "pipelining is not supported on a tail-called answer", ...). sendReturnResultsSentElsewhere already does this. Also record the answered `yourself` id until its Finish, so that a call pipelined on it later fails fast (fail_broken_answer) instead of being queued. Each failed W then goes through its mark: W0 gets one exception, and the wire gets one resultsSentElsewhere. A fuller fix is to keep cap-bearing `yourself` results as a resolved answer so that pipelining works as in C++. Commit the three probes as tests.

handleReturnFrom's stash and hold lookup (mod.zig:6046-6056) does not check `origin`. A loopback `takeFromOtherQuestion` (forwardResolvedCall `.sent_elsewhere` for one of our own loopback calls, mod.zig:3351) names OUR outbound question id. The stash and `send_results_to_yourself` are keyed by the remote's question ids, and both counters start at 0. So a numeric collision could hold the loopback question on an unrelated remote call and give it that call's results. Reachability is not verified: it needs a loopback call to a promise export that resolved to a promised answer. Consider limiting the lookup to origin == .transport. The stash half is pre-existing. The hold, and now the cancelled-question hold, make it wider.

sendPrebuiltReturnFrame clears the sendResultsTo routing (the mark) before reserveResolvedAnswer and the send (peer_return_send.zig:445). On an OOM there, a hold stays with no mark. A retry through the unmarked sendReturnResults or sendReturnException path never calls releaseHeldTailCall, so the question waits for a Finish(Y) that C++ sends only after Finish(X). Release the hold in an errdefer, or clear the routing after the send, as clearAndSendReturnFrameForPeer does.

`.propagate_results_sent_elsewhere` relays a forwarded `canceled` through sendReturnTag(.canceled) (peer_forwarded_return_logic.zig:112). That skips releaseHeldTailCall on the assumption that the remote already finished Y, which is not true here. It is reachable only from a remote that returns `canceled` without our Finish (non-compliant), so this is low priority, but the `tag != .canceled` shortcut could instead check whether Y is still in active_inbound_questions.

Pre-existing, now more likely: routeCall's noteSendResultsToYourself can fail on the max_send_results_to_yourself bound, which now also counts parked and queued calls. The refused `yourself` call then gets an exception Return on the wire, which C++ treats as a protocol error. Answer such a refusal with resultsSentElsewhere directly, or list it in docs/native-abi.md next to the bounds.

958283c restores the mark with a plain `put` that skips the count bound. This is trivial. After a failed resultsSentElsewhere send for a held call, the follow-up exception is stashed under Y although Y's redirect was already used. The entry is bounded and dropped on id reuse, so it is harmless now, but a comment would help.

Pre-existing: in the C++ order for a question cancelled before its redirect (our Finish(X), then the remote's Finish(Y), then the host's answer), the host's late answer goes on the wire as a plain `results` Return for a `yourself` call, because Finish removed the mark. A probe printed 'wire Returns Y=1 rse=0'. C++ accepts it, since the question was already cancelled (rpc.c++ else-branch at :4100), but rpc.capnp says resultsSentElsewhere. The behaviour is correct and needs no change; it could be pinned in a test.

Verified correct: a question cancelled and held sends exactly one Finish(X), at cancel time, and none at the held delivery (probe 'cancel-finish: Finish(X) frames=1'). Finish(Y) arriving first retires the cancelled question. Drop-on-reuse sits after the DuplicateQuestionId check and cannot drop an entry that a pending redirect still needs, because the remote reuses Y only after Finish(Y), which follows the redirect. Loopback ids descend from the top of the id space, so loopback Calls do not drop remote stash entries.

must_fix.issue: A held tail call can now hang for good. This happens when the yourself call it names is parked on a promise export and the remote then releases that export. Since 908314b, routeCall marks a yourself call as soon as it arrives, so a redirect that names a parked call is held. But destroyExportEntry frees the parked calls without sending any Return, and it does not touch the yourself mark or the hold. The held question then waits for a call that will never be answered. Nothing settles it except capnp_cancel, a deadline or a transport close. A compliant remote sends Finish for the named call only after this question's Finish, which can never come. The host cannot settle it either: capnp_reject_promise on the freed export returns UnknownExport. On main, and on this branch before 908314b, the redirect for a parked call is not held, so the question gets its one Return at once (the bare tag; on the native side, the 'unsupported Return variant' or unfollowed exception) and sends its Finish.

nice_to_have: OOM while a held question is being given its answer: I ran a one-allocation-failure sweep (probe 'PROBE r3: one-allocation-failure sweep'). It covers 13 scenarios: plain hold, parked then resolve, parked then reject, parked then Finish, cancel before the redirect then Finish, cancel while held then Finish, cancel then id reuse, forward back to the remote, stash then reuse, failed send, unknown capability, Finish during build. I ran each with one-shot and with sticky failure at every allocation index, using a fresh DebugAllocator for each run. In every run nothing leaked, nothing was freed twice, and every question had exactly one Return after deinit. Sticky mode showed no anomalies. One-shot mode found these: (a) An OOM inside deliverHeldTailCall, settleTailCallOnFinish or releaseHeldTailCall leaves the question waiting. The hold is taken before the frame is built or decoded, so the failure is only reported. This is documented in docs/native-abi.md. A cheap improvement: build the tail_call_finished frame and the bare-redirect frame in a stack buffer, with the same BufferFirstAllocator pattern deliverLocalException uses (H8). (b) parked_reject at fail_index 81-86: buildReturnExceptionFrame in completeSelfLoopbackException fails inside the replayResolvedPromiseExport drain, and the drain swallows the error. The call gets no wire Return and its question stays held. Main also sent no Return for the call, but there the question got the bare tag.

After a failed resultsSentElsewhere send for a held tail call, 958283c puts the mark back. The deferred delivery has already given the question the results. The host's follow-up exception then finds no hold and stashes the exception. My probe 'failsend' shows returns=1, stash=1. The entry is harmless: it is bounded, and it is dropped on id reuse or at deinit. But it is the kind of stale entry 3af5559 tries to avoid. A redirect plus a Finish(Y) that both arrive during `build` (held_before_build=false) also leave one stale entry.

handleFinish registers `errdefer self.settleTailCallOnFinish(qid)` at src/rpc/peer/mod.zig:4849. That is after `_ = try self.cancelQueuedPendingQuestion(...)` at :4815, which has already cleared the call's yourself mark through sendReturnTag(.canceled). If an error follows that send (for example `try empty_keys.append` at :4981 fails with OOM), the hold stays with no mark. Register the errdefer at the top of handleFinish; settleTailCallOnFinish is idempotent.

In settleSelfLoopbackAnswer, the mark is restored in the catch block before the deferred held delivery runs. The held question's callback can send Finish(X) on a synchronous transport. The remote's Finish(Y) then removes the restored mark, and the host's follow-up capnp_return_exception goes on the wire as an exception Return for the tail call. This needs a failed send and a synchronous transport at the same time, so it is niche. Doing the delivery before the restore, or checking the mark again in the follow-up, would close it.

Pre-existing, now as two resultsSentElsewhere Returns instead of an exception plus resultsSentElsewhere. In forwardResolvedCall (src/rpc/peer/mod.zig:3326-3352), the forwarded call goes on the wire first, and then finishForwardResolvedCall can fail (OOM in forwarded_questions.put). The catch in handleResolvedCall answers Y, and the forwarded Return later answers Y again. In the one-shot sweep, forward_rse at fail_index=92 gives rse=2 for answer 900.

Documented and the same as on main: if noteSendResultsToYourself fails (OOM or the max_send_results_to_yourself bound) in routeCall, the call is still answered with a plain exception Return. The C++ reference rejects that Return for its tail call. The sweep hits this at the first allocation after the call arrives, in every scenario. Since parked calls now hold marks too, parked yourself calls count toward that bound.

Pre-existing: a call parked on a promise export loses its Return when the export is destroyed, for every sendResultsTo kind, and its active_inbound_questions entry then reserves that id until deinit. The must-fix above is the tail-call form of this defect; fixing it at the root closes both.

fixed: Must-fix 1 and 3 (the same defect: a parked call is dropped when the remote releases its promise export, so the held tail call hangs). Fixed in 06035f3. destroyExportEntry's deinit_pending_call hook in src/rpc/peer/peer_export_release.zig (answerDroppedParkedCall) now answers each parked call with sendReturnException(question_id, rpc.peer.promise_export_released_reason) and then releases its inbound caps. Nothing is sent while in_deinit. The draining send also fails calls pipelined on the dropped call. A `yourself` call answers resultsSentElsewhere and gives the held question the exception. The pre-existing gaps are closed too: any parked call now gets its Return, and its param import refs are released. Red, then green, then red with the hook ablated. A second ablation (no releaseInboundCaps) turns the param-Release assertion red. Peer tests in tests/rpc/peer/rpc_reflected_direct_handler_test.zig: a held tail call whose parked call loses its export to a Release (the realistic flow: the promise is passed in params so ref_count=1, then a yourself Call, the redirect, Release); the Release before the redirect; and a plain parked call with a senderHosted param plus a call pipelined on it. Native test in src/native/conn_test.zig: the C++ tailCall-then-Release pattern; afterwards rejectPromise returns UnknownExport.

Must-fix 2 (a call pipelined on a tail-called answer is never answered, so W0 hangs). Fixed in 543e642 in src/rpc/peer/return/peer_return_send.zig. completeSelfLoopbackReturn now fails the calls queued on the answer with the new rpc.peer.tail_call_pipelining_reason (failTailCalledPipeline; it runs only when pending_promises holds the id, so the OOM harness test stays clean). Every answered `yourself` call is now recorded in failed_answers until its Finish (recordTailCalledAnswer), so a later pipelined call fails at once through fail_broken_answer. Results record that reason; exceptions record their own exception. The record is taken before the resultsSentElsewhere send, and only while the call is active and not loopback. A remote Finish inside the send therefore removes it, and a failed send drops it. The same record and drain also run for a forwarded `yourself` call answered by sendReturnTag(resultsSentElsewhere) or sendReturnTakeFromOtherQuestion. That variant was the same regression and was not in the review. Tests, each red before the fix: queued before the answer, arriving after it, a failed tail call, a receiverAnswer param, the forwarded rse path, the forwarded takeFromOtherQuestion path, and a Finish inside the send (guard), plus the native bounce in both orders. Ablations that each turned tests red: the drain, the record, the active check, recording after the send, and the forwarded tail_called checks.

Must-fix 3 follow-up (does the replay drain drop a Return?). For handler errors it does not. handleResolvedExportedCall (peer_call_orchestration.zig:60) already turns a replayed handler's error into an exception Return. Commit aae3b3a pins this with two guard tests: a held tail call, and a plain parked call whose handler fails on replay. Both go red when that catch is ablated. The remaining case, an OOM in the drain's frame decode or in its exception send, is documented in docs/native-abi.md and the CHANGELOG hold entry rather than fixed.
rejected: The reviewer's line 'handleResolvedCallReportingErrors only reports' is not a real Return-loss for handler errors. Before that wrapper is reached, handleResolvedExportedCall catches the error and sends sendReturnException. The proof is aae3b3a: the guard tests pass on the unchanged code and fail with that catch removed. Only an allocation failure inside the drain can still drop a Return, and that is documented, not fixed.

open_issues: Behaviour change, documented in CHANGELOG: an answered `yourself` call now keeps its id in use until the remote's Finish, as any answer does. A new Call with that id before the Finish gets DuplicateQuestionId. I updated the fuzz-found test in tests/rpc/peer/rpc_peer_test.zig ('stash does not leak on duplicate answer id') to expect the refusal before Finish and a clean reuse after it. C++ and Zig peers reuse ids only after Finish, so compliant remotes are not affected.

New limit, documented: a call that passes a tail-called answer as a receiverAnswer param now fails with tail_call_pipelining_reason, as for a failed answer. It used to dispatch with an unusable .promised entry, which the native shim already refused with PromisedCapUnsupported. Pipelining on cap-bearing tail-call results is still unsupported (the C++ reference supports it).

Documented, not fixed: an OOM in the replay drain (frame decode, or an exception send it reports) or in delivering a held answer still leaves the question waiting until a cancel, its deadline or a transport close.

Not addressed (reviewers' nice-to-haves): the handleFinish errdefer placement, sendPrebuiltReturnFrame clearing routing before the send, the mark restore racing a synchronous Finish(Y), the origin check in handleReturnFrom's stash lookup, a forwarded `canceled` skipping releaseHeldTailCall, and pre-existing gaps where calls queued on non-yourself answers that end with takeFromOtherQuestion, acceptFromThirdParty or a prebuilt exception are never drained.

Not run: the e2e docker lanes and cross-implementation interop. Nothing is pushed (as instructed); the branch sprint/p1-3-native-tail-call is 4 commits ahead of 18d8138 in /Users/nullstyle/prj/zig/capnp-zig/.claude/worktrees/wf_96205a35-f41-2.

must_fix.issue: A question X whose takeFromOtherQuestion names a `yourself` call Y is held forever when the Peer forwards Y back to the remote (Y targets one of our promise exports that resolves to the remote's capability). The C++ reference never answers a forwarded `yourself` call by itself, so X never gets a Return, sends no Finish, and the flow deadlocks. Y is now marked when it arrives (908314b), so holdTailCall holds X on it. In `.propagate_results_sent_elsewhere` mode the Peer forwards Y as Y' with sendResultsTo = yourself. The hold is released only when Y is answered (releaseHeldTailCall in sendReturnTag, bcd87fd, or the drain in 543e642), and that happens only after the remote sends a Return for Y'. A C++ (or Rust capnp-rpc) callee keeps a `yourself` call's results in `answer.task` (Redirected). It sends the resultsSentElsewhere Return only when a takeFromOtherQuestion names Y', or when the call context is destroyed at Finish(Y'). capnp-zig sends neither: propagate mode does not register forwarded_tail_questions, so Finish(Y) is never relayed to Y', and Y' is auto-finished only after its Return. The C++ side sends Finish(Y) only after Finish(X), and X is held. The result is a cycle that only a cancel, a deadline or a transport close ends. On main the question ended at once with the bare tag (native: one EXCEPTION RETURN). The branch's own claims fail here. CHANGELOG.md:44-48 says the question "does not wait for the remote's Finish" and gets the bare tag "as soon as that Return is sent". docs/native-abi.md:56 and :88 say the RETURN comes "when the forwarded call returns". Against the reference implementation, that never happens.

C++: vendor/ext/capnproto/c++/src/capnp/rpc.c++:3893-3897 (a redirected call's task keeps the results and sends no Return), :3300 sendRedirectReturn (called only from the take handlers at :4082 and :4114), :3158-3180 (~RpcCallContext sends resultsSentElsewhere when the task is dropped at Finish, :4153). The tests that encode non-reference remote behaviour: tests/rpc/peer/rpc_reflected_direct_handler_test.zig:1111 and :1128, and src/native/conn_test.zig:2246. Each pushes an eager Return(forwarded, resultsSentElsewhere/exception) that a C++ callee never sends.
must_fix.why: This breaks liveness and the 'exactly one Return per question' rule. X gets zero Returns, and the call it names never completes. A native host (capnp-swift) waits forever unless it cancels or sets a deadline. Main does not hang here. The same commit series treats C++ tail calls into our promise exports as a realistic flow (06035f3). This variant only needs the host to resolve the promise to a C++ capability instead of the remote releasing it. A second variant needs no host action: Y arrives after the promise was already resolved to an import (C++ sent it before it processed our Resolve), Y is forwarded at once, and the redirect that follows is held.

must_fix.suggested_fix: A forwarded `yourself` call never brings its results back to this peer, so stop waiting for its answer. (a) In Peer.forwardResolvedCall, after the forward is sent in propagate_results_sent_elsewhere mode, call releaseHeldTailCall(call.question_id). (b) Make holdTailCall return false for a call that has been forwarded (for example, look it up in forwarded_questions, or keep a small set). A prototype of (a) and (b) in scratchpad/p13r4lens/fixproto turns both probes green: X gets the bare redirect (native: unfollowed_tail_call_reason), and Finish(X) is sent. It changes only the 2 Peer tests and 1 native test that push the eager forwarded Return; their expectations would move to 'bare redirect at forward time'. Optionally, and this part is pre-existing: relay Finish(Y) to Y' in propagate mode, so the C++ callee drops its context and sends Return(Y', resultsSentElsewhere), and Y gets its own resultsSentElsewhere. Then fix CHANGELOG.md:44-48 and docs/native-abi.md:56/:88, and add a test where the remote answers the forwarded yourself call only after its Finish.

nice_to_have: Pre-existing (main has it too): in propagate_results_sent_elsewhere mode, Finish(Y) is never relayed to the forwarded Y' (peer_forward_orchestration.zig:157 registers forwarded_tail_questions only for sent_elsewhere/translate_to_caller). Against C++, Y' therefore never returns and Y never gets a Return. The C++ question-table entry for Y, our Y' question and its ForwardCallContext all leak until disconnect.

Pre-existing design gap that the branch makes deterministic: the C++ pattern from the commit message (`return context.tailCall(p.fooRequest())` with P passed in X's params) now always fails with promise_export_released_reason, because C++ releases P (callNoIntercept/releaseParams) before the host resolves it. A C++ callee keeps the promise alive for its queued calls, so the same flow succeeds between two C++ peers. Pin the promise export while calls are parked on it (a parked-call ref class next to promise_ref_count) and answer with the exception only when nobody can resolve it any more. Today the CHANGELOG states the divergence honestly.

Marking a `yourself` call when it arrives (routeCall, peer_call_inbound.zig:175) can fail: max_send_results_to_yourself is full, or OutOfMemory. The catch then sends an exception Return on the wire for a tail call, which C++ rejects at rpc.c++:4055 and drops the connection. Marks now live for the whole time a call is parked, so this bound is easier to hit than on main, where marks were taken only at dispatch. When the mark fails, answer resultsSentElsewhere anyway; the redirect then gets the bare tag.

Behaviour change (543e642): a Call whose params carry a receiverAnswer that names an answered `yourself` call now fails as a whole with tail_call_pipelining_reason, through resolvePromisedParamCaps and lookupFailedAnswer. On main it dispatched, with an unusable .promised entry. It is documented, but C++ would dispatch with a working pipeline cap. Consider failing only the param capability, as the failed-answer note in prepareParamCapsForDispatch already suggests for C++ parity.

answerDroppedParkedCall sends Returns and runs held-question callbacks (deliverHeldTailCall -> handleReturn) from inside destroyExportEntry. That code runs during handleFinish's answer-held cap release, inside handleReturn's consumeQuestionParamExports, and before finalizeExportRelease. finalizeExportRelease returns early if `exports.contains(id)`. A callback that re-registers the same id (addExportAt, where the native host owns the id space) would skip the promise-held and import-pin cleanup. The probability is low. Defer the hook's sends until finalizeExportRelease has run, or note that it re-enters there.

nice_to_have: The fix in 3af5559 misses one case. src/rpc/peer/return/peer_return_send.zig:209 drops the built results only when a hold existed BEFORE `build`. If the redirect and then Finish(Y) both arrive during `build`, the hold is made and settled inside the build: X gets tail_call_finished_reason, but the results are still stashed for a redirect that is already used up. Probe 'REVIEW probe: redirect and Finish both arrive during the build' prints `stash=1`. The entry is harmless: it is bounded, dropped on id reuse or at deinit, and only a second redirect naming Y could take it. A simpler and complete condition: keep nothing when the yourself mark is gone after `build`, because a Finish happened, and per rpc.capnp no redirect follows Finish(Y). Not a regression.

answerDroppedParkedCall (src/rpc/peer/peer_export_release.zig:483) now sends Returns and can run question callbacks: held-tail delivery, loopback questions, the pipelined drain. It runs inside destroyExportEntry (peer_cap_lifecycle.zig:249), before finalizeExportRelease and the export's deinit_ctx. Every release path reaches it: handleRelease, consumeQuestionParamExports inside handleReturnFrom, the Finish answer-held cleanup, stream_dispatch.releasePending, and cross-peer `source_peer.releaseHandoffHeldExport`. My probes of the realistic paths (Release, then Finish of the answer that held P; releaseParamCaps on the redirect itself) are clean under the testing allocator. Still, collecting the detached calls and answering them after finalizeExportRelease returns would shrink a callback window this branch makes new.

OOM: a single transient allocation failure can leave a tail call unanswered. My one-shot sweeps found these cases. (a) The yourself call gets no Return at all when answerDroppedParkedCall's exception or resultsSentElsewhere send fails: nobody sends a follow-up answer, so the mark restore from 958283c does not help. (b) X stays held until a cancel, deadline or close when failQueuedPromisedCalls cannot seed its worklist. The CHANGELOG and native-abi.md describe this OOM wait in general terms, so this is acceptable. The ALLOC_FAIL sweeps found no leaks, double frees or crashes.

sendReturnAcceptFromThirdParty (peer_return_send.zig:898) releases a hold but does not record or drain the answer, unlike the other two forwarded-yourself paths fixed in 543e642 (sendReturnTag resultsSentElsewhere and sendReturnTakeFromOtherQuestion). Suppose a parked yourself call is forwarded and the remote answers the forward with awaitFromThirdParty. Then calls pipelined on Y still queue forever. It is rare (L3 plus a tail call), but it is the same class as the round-3 must-fix 2.

Doc nit: the loopback_result_stash field doc (src/rpc/peer/mod.zig:768) still says the forwarder's Finish of the forwarded question can arrive BEFORE the takeFromOtherQuestion. The id-reuse drop added in 5f8b40a relies on the opposite: the redirect comes before Finish(Y). The Zig forwarder sends the redirect eagerly and relays Finish(Y) only on Finish(X) (peer_forward_orchestration.zig finishForwardResolvedCall). Reword the doc so the two comments agree.

Doc nit: the yourself records from 543e642 share the failed_answers count bound (max_active_inbound_questions, peer_return_send.zig recordFailedAnswer) with real failed answers. Many tail calls in flight can therefore skip records, and the pipelined calls then hang, without any memory pressure. The CHANGELOG mentions only 'under memory pressure'.

Pre-existing: an OOM on the arrival mark (routeCall, peer_call_inbound.zig:175; the one-shot sweep hit it at fail_at=3) still sends an exception Return for a yourself call. The C++ reference rejects that. main does the same at dispatch, and the code comment says so.

Pre-existing, synchronous-transport only: the fail_broken_answer path passes a borrowed failed_answers[A].reason into sendReturnExceptionTyped. That reason is then used after the send (failQueuedPromisedCalls at peer_return_send.zig:569, and recordFailedAnswer on the non-yourself path). A Finish(A) re-entered inside that send frees it. Duplicating the reason before the send would close this.

Design limit, documented: a promise export with parked calls is destroyed when the remote drops its wire refs. The C++ reference keeps the queued call alive through the call's own reference. So `tailCall(p.foo())` on a promise the host passed now fails fast with promise_export_released_reason instead of running when the host resolves p. Letting parked calls pin the export, for example with a pending-call ref class, would match the C++ behavior.

- A parked call is always unanswered: a Finish removes it from the list.

fixed: MUST-FIX (protocol lens, regression), fixed in a9f73ad: a question X whose takeFromOtherQuestion names a `yourself` call Y was held forever when the Peer forwarded Y back to the remote. Red first: 5 Peer tests in tests/rpc/peer/rpc_reflected_direct_handler_test.zig and 1 native test in src/native/conn_test.zig, covering both reviewer probes plus a pipelined variant. Fix: Peer.forwardResolvedCall calls the new ReturnSend.noteYourselfCallForwarded(Y) in .propagate_results_sent_elsewhere mode. That function records Y as tail-called, fails calls pipelined on Y with tail_call_pipelining_reason, and releases the hold, so X gets the bare redirect (native: unfollowed_tail_call_reason) and Finish(X) is sent. holdTailCall refuses a source that is the upstream of a forwarded_questions entry, the same scan isForwardedAnswer does. That check is also load-bearing for the release: the bare redirect re-enters handleReturn and would otherwise be held again on the still-marked Y. In propagate mode the forwarded call's exception now also answers Y resultsSentElsewhere, so nothing is stashed for a redirect that already ended. Ablation, each part removed in turn: the forward-time note (4 Peer tests + the native test red), the holdTailCall check (3 Peer + 2 native red), the release (2 red), the pipeline drain (1 red), the record (1 red), the exception arm (1 red). Tests at :1111, :1128 and native :2246 now expect the bare redirect at forward time. New tests: a call forwarded before its redirect (Peer and native), and a call pipelined on a parked yourself call that is then forwarded. The second is a variant I found: W pipelined on Y, with W0 held on W, deadlocked the same way.

Same must-fix, docs: CHANGELOG.md (the Changed entry formerly at :44-48 and the pipelining Fixed entry), docs/native-abi.md (table row :56 and the paragraph formerly at :88, now 'when the call is forwarded'), plus the held_tail_calls, failed_answers and recordTailCalledAnswer doc comments.

Optional, pre-existing part of the same finding, fixed in 34efe40: Finish(Y) is now relayed to Y' in propagate mode. finishForwardResolvedCall registers forwarded_tail_questions and suppresses Y''s auto-finish (not for a loopback upstream, which never gets a Finish). If Y' has not returned at the remote's Finish of Y, sendTailFinishAndNeutralize answers Y with resultsSentElsewhere (the new ReturnSend.answerFinishedForwardedCall, matching C++ ~RpcCallContext) and fails calls still queued on Y. The late Return of Y' is absorbed. This is the test the reviewer asked for, where the remote answers the forwarded yourself call only after its Finish (Peer and native). There are also tests for a remote that answers at once, a call queued with the failed-answer records full, and a loopback forward (rpc_peer_from_peer_zig_test). Ablation: no relay (3 red + native red), relay without answering Y (2 red), no drain (1 red), no loopback exclusion (unit test + the loopback test red). CHANGELOG gets a new Fixed entry and native-abi.md a new sentence.

Reviewer-2 nice-to-have, fixed in 7e9961d: when a redirect and then Finish(Y) both arrived during the results build, a stale stash entry was left. Now nothing is kept when the yourself mark is gone after the build. New red test; the ablation turns it and the existing held-before-build test red.

Doc nits, fixed in 7004322 and a6b1676: the loopback_result_stash doc no longer claims a Finish can come before the redirect. The CHANGELOG line that 2a768bd left at 110 columns is rewrapped. The CHANGELOG now says the tail-call failed-answer record is also skipped at the max_active_inbound_questions bound, not only under memory pressure.
rejected: Reviewer-2 nice-to-have 'sendReturnAcceptFromThirdParty releases a hold but does not record or drain; a forwarded yourself call answered with awaitFromThirdParty leaves pipelined calls queued forever': this cannot happen as described. In propagate mode (the only mode with a marked yourself upstream) the awaitFromThirdParty arm calls send_return_tag(resultsSentElsewhere), which records and drains, and it did before this branch too. sendReturnAcceptFromThirdParty is reached only by translate mode (caller-tag upstream, never marked) and propagate_accept mode (noteSendResultsToThirdParty removes the yourself mark). Since a9f73ad the record and drain for a forwarded yourself call also happen at forward time.

Found while reading, not fixed: a LOOPBACK question (sendCallResolved on our own promise export) whose promise resolved to an import is forwarded in translate_to_caller mode. That registers forwarded_tail_questions and suppresses the forward's auto-finish, but a completed loopback answer never gets a Finish. A temporary probe, since removed, showed that after the forward returns: Finish(forwarded)=0, forwarded_tail_questions=1, inboundAnswerQuestionIdInUse(q)=true. The forward leaks on both ends until the Peer is torn down. The code predates this branch; I did not run the probe on e9f37e1.

Pre-existing, not fixed (both reviewers): if marking a `yourself` call when it arrives fails (max_send_results_to_yourself full, or OOM), routeCall's catch sends an exception Return for the tail call, which the C++ reference rejects. Marks now live while a call is parked, so the bound is easier to hit than on main.

Pre-existing, not fixed: the fail_broken_answer path passes a borrowed failed_answers[A].reason into sendReturnExceptionTyped. That reason is read again after the send (recordFailedAnswer, failQueuedPromisedCalls). On a synchronous transport, a Finish(A) re-entered inside the send frees it, a use-after-free read. The fix is to dupe the reason in peer_call_orchestration.zig before the send.

Design limits, not changed: a promise export with parked calls is destroyed when the remote releases it, while C++ keeps the queued call alive. So `tailCall(p.foo())` on a promise the host passed fails with promise_export_released_reason. And a receiverAnswer param that names an answered yourself call fails the whole call (from 543e642).
Not changed: answerDroppedParkedCall still sends Returns and runs held-question callbacks inside destroyExportEntry, before finalizeExportRelease. That is the re-entrancy window both reviewers noted.

Behaviour change in 34efe40 to note: a propagate-mode forward that the remote answers at once (capnp-zig's own behaviour) is now finished at the remote's Finish of the upstream call, not on its own Return, as the other forwarding modes already were. e2e-self and the cpp lane are green, but no interop lane reaches a forwarded yourself call. e2e-l3-vatc, the go/python/rust lanes, Linux and Windows runtime were not run.
